newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania interbank leu flat, money market rates up.
newsitem.headline: Romania interbank leu flat, money market rates up.

text.p: Romania's leu currency on Wednesday closed steady at 6,050/6,080 to the dollar on an interbank market still facing hard currency shortages.
Operators said although some hard currency owners had appeared on the market lately the volumes had been too small to smooth interbank trading.
"We are still struggling to cope with dollar squeezes. Sellers don't yet see the current leu-dollar level as an attractive price," said a trader with one of the dealer banks.
Some traders said the leu might slide gradually to 6,200 in the coming days. Retail prices were close to this level.
Traders said the market was anxiously awaiting details on a reform package proposed by the new coalition government. The package is currently being discussed with international lenders.
No official forecasts for 1997 economic indicators have been issued so far. Local bankers said talks with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank were unlikely to end this week.

One-week rates edged up towards 80 percent from some 75-76 percent in early trading with money market traders saying two major players were hungry for leu funds. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
